name: ghidra-bizhawk-mcp
description: Unified Ghidra + BizHawk MCP server for static analysis, P-code emulation, multi-console ROM triage, and live emulation.
long_description:
Connects Ghidra's headless static analysis with BizHawk's live emulation for retro-reversing and firmware analysis. Supports NES, SNES, GBA, NDS, Switch, PSX, Genesis, SMS, Dreamcast and more.

**Features:**
- Decompilation, disassembly, byte search, and binary diffing
- P-code micro-emulation via Ghidra's EmulatorHelper
- Function fingerprinting and signature transfer
- Live BizHawk emulation control (memory read/write, joypad, frame advance, save states)
- Retro console platform detection by magic bytes

ghidra_install_dir.title: Ghidra Installation Directory
ghidra_install_dir.description: Path to your Ghidra installation (e.g. C:\Program Files\ghidra_11.2 or /opt/ghidra)

bizhawk_exe_path.title: BizHawk Emulator Path
bizhawk_exe_path.description: Optional path to EmuHawk.exe for live emulation. Leave blank for Ghidra-only mode.

mock_mode.title: Mock Mode
mock_mode.description: Enable mock mode for zero-dependency environments (disables Ghidra/BizHawk connections). Enabled by default if GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR is not provided.

tools.name: ghidra_analyze
tools.description: Import and analyze a binary into a named Ghidra session. Creates or replaces a session. Returns session_id, platform info, and function count. Call this first before any other Ghidra analysis tool.

tools.name: ghidra_sessions
tools.description: List all active Ghidra session workspaces with their session IDs, binary paths, and load timestamps. Useful before calling ghidra_session_close or ghidra_diff.

tools.name: ghidra_session_close
tools.description: Close and remove a Ghidra session workspace, freeing project resources. Cannot be undone. Use ghidra_sessions first to find active session IDs.

tools.name: ghidra_decompile
tools.description: Decompile a function by name or hex address. Returns decompiled C code. Use after session.analyze has loaded a binary.

tools.name: ghidra_decompile_paginated
tools.description: Decompile a function with line range, token budget, and optional summarization to prevent context-window exhaustion on large functions. Use for functions over 50 lines.

tools.name: ghidra_data_types
tools.description: List all data types defined in the loaded program, including structures, enums, and typedefs. Useful for understanding the program's type landscape before creating new types.

tools.name: ghidra_cross_references
tools.description: Get cross-references to and from a given address. Shows what references the address and what the address references. Useful for understanding how data or code is used across the binary.

tools.name: ghidra_call_graph
tools.description: Get the call graph for a function — shows which functions it calls (callees) and which functions call it (callers). Use after ghidra_decompile to understand function relationships.

tools.name: ghidra_decompile_entrypoints
tools.description: Composite tool that bulk-decompiles all entry points in one call — program entry, exports, main, _start, etc. Use early in analysis to get an overview of the binary's surface area.

tools.name: ghidra_report
tools.description: Produce a Markdown summary of the active workspace — functions, entry points, custom symbols, recovered structures, renamed functions, and comment count. Replaces a GUI CodeBrowser window. Call at the end of a session.

tools.name: ghidra_rename
tools.description: Rename a function or label at a given address. Changes are stored in the Ghidra project database. Use to replace auto-generated names with meaningful identifiers.

tools.name: ghidra_comment
tools.description: Attach a comment to a code unit at a given address. Supports comment types: plate, pre, post, eol, repeatable. Use to document reverse-engineering findings inline.

tools.name: ghidra_create_struct
tools.description: Create a custom structured data type from a JSON member layout. Each member specifies offset (optional), field name, and type string.

tools.name: ghidra_retype
tools.description: Change a local variable or function parameter's type annotation in the decompiled view. Use to replace generic types with meaningful types for cleaner decompilation.

tools.name: ghidra_disassemble
tools.description: Disassemble N raw instructions at an address. Returns mnemonic, operands, hex bytes, and length for each instruction. Use for precise lower-level inspection when decompiled C is insufficient.

tools.name: ghidra_search
tools.description: Search the entire loaded binary for a hex byte pattern. Returns matching addresses with context bytes and any string labels at the hit.

tools.name: ghidra_listing
tools.description: Return a raw hex + ASCII dump for a byte range, equivalent to Ghidra's Listing panel. Complements ghidra_disassemble for data regions.

tools.name: ghidra_diff
tools.description: Compare two loaded sessions by function name and body size. Returns functions unique to each side and functions that changed between versions.

tools.name: ghidra_emulate
tools.description: Headlessly execute a slice of instructions using Ghidra's P-code emulator. Seed initial register values and track value propagation. No debugger or network needed. Works on ARM, x86, MIPS, and any Ghidra-supported architecture.

tools.name: ghidra_emulate_taint
tools.description: Execute an instruction slice with automatic taint tracking. Specify a taint register; the tool reports every step where its value is modified or propagates.

tools.name: ghidra_emulate_breakpoints
tools.description: Execute instructions until a break condition is met or the instruction count expires. Supports equality (R0==0), inequality (R1>0xFF), not-equal (R2!=R3), and PC address (PC==0x1234).

tools.name: ghidra_fingerprint
tools.description: Generate a behavior-based structural hash for a function that survives compiler shuffling across binary versions.

tools.name: ghidra_export_signatures
tools.description: Export a complete {structural_hash -> function_name} signature map for every function in the current binary. Save to reuse across versions.

tools.name: ghidra_apply_signatures
tools.description: Scan the current binary, match every function by structural fingerprint against a previously exported signature map, and rename matches automatically.

tools.name: ghidra_stash_save
tools.description: Fingerprint all functions and stash the signature map server-side under a lineage_group_id label. No JSON files to manage.

tools.name: ghidra_stash_restore
tools.description: Load a previously stashed signature map by lineage_group_id and auto-rename every matching function in the current session.

tools.name: ghidra_stash_auto_save
tools.description: Zero-input auto-stash: hashes the loaded binary's first 4 KB and saves a signature map under that hash. No user input needed.

tools.name: ghidra_stash_auto_restore
tools.description: Zero-input auto-restore: hashes the loaded binary, looks up a previously stashed map by content hash, and renames matching functions automatically.

tools.name: ghidra_stash_list
tools.description: List all stashed signature groups currently in the local server cache (~/.ghidra_bizhawk_mcp/signatures/).

tools.name: ghidra_triage
tools.description: Examines raw file magic header signatures to detect retro console architectures (NES, SNES, GBA, NDS, Switch, PSX, Genesis, SMS, Dreamcast), maps correct Ghidra language loaders, and applies signature caching.

tools.name: bizhawk_connect
tools.description: Check connectivity to BizHawk by pinging the bridge.lua script running inside EmuHawk. Use first before any other bizhawk_* tool.

tools.name: bizhawk_info
tools.description: Get ROM name, ROM hash, framecount, memory domains, and capabilities from the connected BizHawk instance.

tools.name: bizhawk_memory_domains
tools.description: List available memory domains for the loaded emulation core (e.g. WRAM, RAM, EWRAM, VRAM).

tools.name: bizhawk_read
tools.description: Read bytes from BizHawk emulated memory. Returns an array of byte values.

tools.name: bizhawk_write
tools.description: Write bytes to BizHawk emulated memory. Use to patch game state or modify emulated hardware registers in real time.

tools.name: bizhawk_buttons
tools.description: Set joypad button state for a player. Buttons object like {A: true, B: true, Start: true}. Runs once; hold by repeating each frame.

tools.name: bizhawk_frame
tools.description: Advance the emulator by N frames. Use to step through execution or apply button inputs over time.

tools.name: bizhawk_pause
tools.description: Pause BizHawk emulation. Use before reading memory to prevent values changing.

tools.name: bizhawk_unpause
tools.description: Unpause BizHawk emulation after a previous pause call.

tools.name: bizhawk_reset
tools.description: Reset the loaded emulation core (reboot the emulated console). All emulated state is lost.

tools.name: bizhawk_screenshot
tools.description: Save a PNG screenshot of the current emulator display to a file path.

tools.name: bizhawk_save_state
tools.description: Save the current emulator state to a file. Captures all CPU registers, memory, and hardware state.

tools.name: bizhawk_load_state
tools.description: Load emulator state from a previously saved savestate file. Restores all CPU, memory, and hardware state.

tools.name: bizhawk_launch
tools.description: Launch BizHawk emulator and connect the bridge. Optionally specify a ROM path to load.

prompts.name: analyze_rom
prompts.description: Guided ROM analysis workflow: triage a retro ROM, decompile entry points, and run initial analysis in one session.
prompts.text: Load the ROM at {rom_path} using ghidra_triage, then decompile its entry points with ghidra_decompile_entrypoints, and generate a report with ghidra_report.

prompts.name: session_workflow
prompts.description: Demonstrates a full reverse-engineering session: load binary, explore functions, analyze call graphs, and generate a report.
prompts.text: Start a RE session: 1) ghidra_analyze a binary, 2) ghidra_decompile key functions, 3) ghidra_call_graph to understand relationships, 4) ghidra_rename and ghidra_comment to document findings, 5) ghidra_report to summarize.

prompts.name: debug_emulation
prompts.description: P-code emulation debugging workflow: set up emulation context, step through instructions, and analyze register/memory state.
prompts.text: Set up P-code emulation at {address} using ghidra_emulate. Step through instructions, inspect register changes, and use ghidra_emulate_breakpoints to find where a specific condition occurs. Session: {session_id}

prompts.name: live_debug
prompts.description: Combined Ghidra + BizHawk workflow: analyze a ROM in Ghidra, connect to BizHawk emulation, and correlate static decompilation with live memory state.
prompts.text: Analyze {rom_path} with ghidra_triage, then decompile key functions. Connect BizHawk with bizhawk_connect, read live memory with bizhawk_read at addresses from Ghidra's analysis, and correlate static decompilation with runtime values.

prompts.name: binary_diff
prompts.description: Compare two binary versions: load both, diff functions, and identify changed or new functions between versions.
prompts.text: Load both binaries into separate Ghidra sessions with ghidra_analyze (paths: {binary_a}, {binary_b}). Then use ghidra_diff to compare function changes between session_a and session_b. Investigate changed functions with ghidra_decompile.
